trigger: pg_advisory_unlock returns non-PGRES_TUPLES_OK on a connection that stays CONNECTION_OK (aborted txn at guard time, or client-side PQexecParams failure); the pg_advisory_unlock_all() fallback then fails identically
summary: Session-advisory-lock release is unsound. Verified on live PG 18.4 by three agents independently: in an aborted txn both the targeted unlock and the unlock_all fallback fail, the lock survives ROLLBACK, and the session stays CONNECTION_OK. PgPool::release (pg_pool.cpp:293-302) checks only PQstatus and rolls back a non-idle txn, so the connection is recycled STILL HOLDING the lock. Session locks are re-entrant per backend, so the poisoned connection's next unlock returns t and the fallback can never fire on it: self-perpetuating, silent, asymmetric wedge of the sole enforcement path for predecessor auto-revoke. The in-code justification ('a failure here means the connection is already unhealthy and PgPool::release()'s own PQstatus check discards it') is false. kek_op_lock.hpp's KekOpLockGuard (#2395) already solved this on the same pool: try/catch the noexcept destructor, discriminate on PQstatus, pg_terminate_backend(pg_backend_pid()).
reporter: cpp-safety / architect A1 / consistency-auditor F2 / cpp-expert F2

trigger: tick N: any routine single-pair rotation elapses, serialising facts 'ew---' and declining. tick N+1: DB clock steps forward below kRotationSweepBigStepSecs (86400), so big_step is false; every pair now elapsed, still no survivor, facts identical
summary: would_wipe = has_expired && !has_survivor is TRUE in the ordinary steady state (verified against live PG by four agents: one in-flight pair, window elapsed => has_expired=t, has_survivor=f). Beyond the false decline, the routine occurrence CONSUMES THE DEDUP SLOT a real anomaly needs: a genuine sub-86400s clock step serialises to the same fact set, is suppressed as a repeat, and drains up to 200 revocations with no decline, no counter and no log. That is the swallowed-anomaly class part 4 of the routed concern exists to close, reached by fact-set collision rather than a latch bool. Corroborated structurally by the change itself: seed_sweep_survivor had to be added to eight existing tests to keep them draining. Reporters derived differently (security-guardian I1 HIGH, consistency-auditor I3 HIGH, cpp-expert I8 LOW, architect SHOULD, sre not-a-finding); max severity taken, and the I1 rests on the swallow mechanism, which only security-guardian identified.

trigger: any pass that holds or cannot obtain the store-wide session lock indefinitely: the lock-release leak above, an orphaned PG backend after host loss (server-side keepalive ~2h, idle_session_timeout off by default), or a drain blocked on contended per-principal locks (lock_timeout 10s x 200 pairs ~ 33min)
summary: A cluster-wide serialisation point was added to a revocation path with no liveness signal. SkippedLock increments a counter and by explicit design never logs; yuzu_engine_principal_rotation_sweep_failures_total stays at zero throughout; no alert rule exists for any rotation_sweep metric. Decisive: in a single-replica deployment (the default) the sweep is one thread taking the lock once per tick and can never legitimately lose the election, so any non-zero SkippedLock is BY CONSTRUCTION a fault -- yet describe() tells the operator it is routine leader-election contention, not a fault. rotation_retention_meta.last_pass_now already IS the durable cluster-wide last-success timestamp such an alert needs; nothing exports it.

adjudication_rationale: Reporter derived LOW/NICE on operational impact. Raising to a policy floor, not lowering: the routed-concern row states this normatively -- a bootstrap decline 'counts to its own ..._retention_bootstrap_declines_total, NEVER the clock-anomaly series, because it asserts only that nothing can yet be ruled out and MUST NOT fire an alert that says the clock moved.' An explicit never/must-not clause in a routed-concern row is a floor by the closed three-source rule and bypasses the derivation. Strengthening the gate, so no independent adjudicator is required.

trigger: operator reads describe() text or the metric family docs for yuzu_rotation_sweep_lock_skipped_total in a single-replica deployment
summary: SkippedLock's documented meaning is wrong, and more specifically wrong than earlier reporters framed it. The sweep's single caller is ONE dedicated thread on a sequential 60s loop, so it cannot self-collide on the session lock. In single-replica -- the default -- a SkippedLock can therefore only mean a SECOND WRITER holding the same Postgres session lock: a zombie process, a botched blue-green cutover, or an unauthorised second server instance pointed at the same DSN. Every comment and the metric's describe() text uniformly frame it as routine leader-election contention, and it is deliberately never logged on any topology. A pilot customer without alerting wired has no way to notice a sustained single-replica lock_skipped.

adjudication_rationale: REFUTED, not rejected: the claim was factually wrong about REACHABILITY and the evidence is an induced negative. Four agents verified the PRIMITIVE in psql (inside an aborted txn both pg_advisory_unlock and pg_advisory_unlock_all fail, the lock survives ROLLBACK, session stays CONNECTION_OK) and then asserted it was reachable through sweep_expired_rotations. It is not: ScopeExit unlock_guard is declared at :2138 and pg::PgTxn txn at :2168, so reverse destruction runs ~PgTxn's ROLLBACK BEFORE the unlock on every early return and on unwinding, and the unlock always executes on a clean connection. Induced by renaming rotation_retention_meta out from under a live store to force a failure inside the classification transaction: outcome=Failed, ZERO advisory locks held anywhere in the database afterwards, recovery tick Ok with the predecessor revoked. Note two of the four reporters recorded the refutation in their own reports without noticing it contradicted their finding -- cpp-expert's verified-clean section states verbatim that 'no aborted transaction can reach the unlock', and architect traced the same destruction order approvingly. The runner relayed both without reconciling them. E6 applies: the wrong outcome is proven unable to occur. The FIX still proceeds at NICE -- the in-code claim that unlock_all() is a working fallback is genuinely false, and adopting the shared guard removes an unpinned correctness dependency on declaration order.

summary: MEASURED: 120 consecutive ticks (2h at the 60s cadence) all returned SkippedLock; the eligible predecessor stayed revoked=f; and validate_token() on the predecessor's RAW SECRET returned the token both at tick 0 and after all 120 ticks -- the rotated-out credential authenticated for the entire outage. trigger: NARROWED from 'any routine single-pair rotation' to '>=6 eligible pairs all past their overlap window in one tick' — a scripted batch rotation with the default uniform overlap, or accumulation via chaos-CH3 whose lost revokes nothing else drains
summary: MEASURED at population 6 by two independent agents: routine batch expiry declines and plants facts 'ew---'; the next tick's genuine 12h forward step (below the 86400s big_step floor) yields the byte-identical fact set, is dedup-suppressed, and revokes 12 predecessors -- six whose windows had NOT elapsed pre-step -- with outcome=Ok, no decline, no counter, no log. A population threshold cannot close this: the defect is a routine verdict spending a single un-namespaced dedup slot, and every population has an all-expired terminal state. The dirty window is also wider than one tick -- the slot survives the drain tick, persists ceil(N/200) ticks on a backlog, and stays dirty INDEFINITELY while failed_pairs>0 keeps the eligible set from shrinking, i.e. permanently under the pool contention chaos-CH3 measured. The constant's own doc justification ('a handful of pairs all expiring in the SAME tick is a materially different signal') was measured to be the ordinary outcome of one scripted batch rotation. ROOT DIAGNOSIS (architect): the probe is mis-fitted at the TYPE level -- audit_store's population is a time series where 100% expiry can only mean the cutoff moved; this store's is a drain queue SUPPOSED to reach 100% expiry. Separately, kRotationSweepBigStepSecs=86400 is audit_store's number on a sweep that re-anchors every 60s, violating the routed concern's own 'copy the SHAPE, never the numbers' -- a 1-day step floor on a 1-minute re-anchor is exactly the sub-86400 hole would_wipe was covering.

adjudication_rationale: REVIEWER DISAGREEMENT ADJUDICATED. sre reviewed the same code and passed it, arguing classify's precedence (BadState>Step>Wipe>NoAnchor) means 'NoAnchor only ever fires alone' so the split is complete. Both agents agree on the mechanism -- when no_anchor and would_wipe co-occur the enum returns Wipe -- and disagree on whether that is correct. Adjudicated FOR security-guardian: the routed concern's stated reason is that a bootstrap decline 'asserts only that nothing can yet be ruled out and must not fire an alert that says the clock moved'. PRE-EXISTING: broken in KekOpLockGuard since #2395, inherited by the extraction -- but this round replaced a false unlock_all safety-net claim with a DIFFERENT false one, and the new claim is the entire recorded justification for creating the shared abstraction. Verified fix: on unlock failure with CONNECTION_OK and PQtransactionStatus != PQTRANS_IDLE, ROLLBACK, retry the unlock, then fall back to terminate -- measured leaked 1 -> 0. Related INFO: the guard pins the release SQL but not the KEY, so a drift in one half of a hand-written lock/unlock pair unlocks a key never locked, Postgres returns false, and the destructor treats false as released -- a silent leak.
